papers.name: Papers 1 to 4 (all content: Breadth in chemistry and Depth in chemistry, Foundation 01/02, Higher 03/04)

topics.name: Chapter C1 Air and water
points: C1.1 The particle model, states of matter and changes of state; physical and chemical change; limitations of the model
C1.1 Formation of the early atmosphere and development of an oxygen-rich atmosphere
C1.1 Atmospheric pollutants (CO, particulates, SO₂, NOx): sources, problems and ways to reduce them
C1.1 Writing formulae and balanced equations; tests for oxygen, hydrogen and carbon dioxide (PAG); oxidation as gain of oxygen
C1.2 Endothermic and exothermic reactions; reaction profiles and activation energy
C1.2 Calculating energy changes from bond breaking and bond making energies
C1.2 Investigating temperature changes in reactions; chemical cells and fuel cells (triple)
C1.3 The greenhouse effect and evidence for human causes of climate change
C1.3 Effects of increased CO₂ and methane and ways to mitigate them
C1.4 Methods of increasing the supply of potable water; test for chlorine (PAG)

topics.name: Chapter C2 Chemical patterns
points: C2.1 Development of the atomic model (Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr)
C2.1 Structure of the atom; protons, neutrons and electrons; size and scale of atoms; atomic and mass numbers
C2.2 Electron arrangement and position in the Periodic Table; Mendeleev's Periodic Table
C2.2 Metals and non-metals; properties and reactions of Group 1 elements
C2.2 Properties and reactions of Group 7 elements; displacement reactions and reactivity trends (PAG1)
C2.3 Group 0 properties; explaining group trends from outer-shell electrons
C2.3 Ionic bonding: electron transfer, dot and cross diagrams, ions
C2.3 Properties of ionic compounds and limitations of representations of ionic structures
C2.4 Formulae of elements and compounds from common ions; balanced equations with state symbols
C2.5 Properties of transition metals (triple)

topics.name: Chapter C3 Chemicals of the natural environment
points: C3.1 Metallic bonding and properties of metals
C3.2 The reactivity series from reactions with water, acid and displacement; ionic equations
C3.2 Extraction of metals using carbon and electrolysis; biological extraction methods
C3.3 Electrolysis of molten ionic compounds; half equations; oxidation and reduction as electron loss and gain
C3.3 Electrolysis of aqueous solutions and competing reactions at electrodes; extraction of aluminium (PAG2)
C3.4 Crude oil as a finite source of hydrocarbons; fractional distillation; alkanes
C3.4 Covalent bonding, dot and cross diagrams, empirical formulae and representations of simple molecules
C3.4 Properties of simple molecules and intermolecular forces; cracking
C3.4 Functional groups and homologous series: alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and their reactions (triple)

topics.name: Chapter C4 Material choices
points: C4.1 Comparing properties of glass, ceramics, polymers, composites and metals to choose materials for uses
C4.1 Composition, properties and uses of alloys such as steel (triple)
C4.2 Addition polymerisation (triple)
C4.2 Condensation polymerisation; DNA and other natural polymers (triple)
C4.3 Explaining bulk properties of materials from bonding and structure; carbon's bonding and organic compounds
C4.3 Bonding in polymers and giant covalent structures; diamond and graphite
C4.4 Nanoparticles: size, surface area to volume ratio, properties and uses
C4.4 Fullerenes and graphene; risks of nanoparticles
C4.5 Corrosion and its prevention by barriers and sacrificial protection (triple)
C4.5 Oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen and electrons
C4.5 Life cycle assessment; reuse and recycling of materials such as PET bottles and metals

topics.name: Chapter C5 Chemical analysis
points: C5.1 Formulations and purity; using melting point data
C5.1 Chromatography: stationary and mobile phases, interpreting chromatograms and Rf values (PAG)
C5.1 Filtration, crystallisation, simple and fractional distillation; choosing purification techniques (PAG3, PAG7)
C5.2 Flame tests and tests for aqueous cations and anions (PAG5) (triple)
C5.2 Emission spectroscopy and advantages of instrumental methods (triple)
C5.3 Conservation of mass; relative formula mass; the mole and Avogadro constant
C5.3 Reacting masses, stoichiometry and limiting reactants
C5.3 Theoretical and percentage yield; molar gas volume (triple)
C5.4 Concentration of solutions in g/dm³ and mol/dm³
C5.4 Neutralisation, H⁺ and OH⁻ ions; titration procedure and evaluating titration data (PAG6)
C5.4 Qualitative vs quantitative analysis; titration calculations relating volumes and concentrations (triple)

topics.name: Chapter C6 Making useful chemicals
points: C6.1 Reactions of acids with metals and carbonates; making salts (PAG7)
C6.1 pH, strong and weak, dilute and concentrated acids; H⁺ concentration and pH
C6.2 Factors affecting rate: temperature, concentration, pressure, surface area; collision theory
C6.2 Catalysts, activation energy and enzymes
C6.2 Measuring rates of reaction and interpreting rate graphs and gradients (PAG8)
C6.3 Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
C6.3 Effects of concentration, temperature and pressure on equilibrium; choosing conditions
C6.4 NPK fertilisers and the importance and costs of the Haber process (triple)
C6.4 Conditions for the Haber process: rate versus equilibrium position (triple)
C6.4 Atom economy and choosing reaction pathways; sustainability (triple)
C6.4 Industrial versus laboratory production of fertilisers; batch and continuous processes (triple)

topics.name: Chapter C7 Ideas about Science
points: IaS1 Planning investigations: hypotheses, apparatus, variables, sample size, risk and communicating methods
IaS2 Presenting data: units, significant figures, graphs and lines of best fit
IaS2 Analysing and evaluating data: means, ranges, outliers, accuracy, precision, repeatability, conclusions
IaS3 Correlation and cause; how explanations develop over time; peer review; using models
IaS4 Applications, risks and benefits of science and technology; ethical issues; communicating science

topics.name: Chapter C8 Practical skills
points: PAG1 Reactivity trend and PAG2 Electrolysis
PAG3 Separation techniques and PAG4 Distillation
PAG5 Identification of species and PAG6 Titration
PAG7 Production of salts and PAG8 Measuring rates of reaction
